title: Compact accepted workload with rename-state names
summary: Accepted Run Once workloads now default to a folded, filename-first view of at most 20 rows, open into the complete exact-identity selection list, and use versioned backend production naming-plan filenames or exact same-job terminal output evidence while preserving immutable accepted labels and raw source paths for proof.
reason: Large accepted workloads made routine Current Work monitoring difficult to scan, and raw release filenames did not match the operator's configured rename state.
behavior_before: Current Work rendered every accepted row as a tall position/path/stage/route card and displayed the raw source leaf name.
behavior_after: Current Work initially renders only the first 20 backend-evidenced filenames as noninteractive preview rows. Opening file selection renders every accepted item as an exact job-ID selectable row, retains selection/focus across same-run refresh, resets safely to the folded disclosure when a different run replaces the workload, restores disclosure focus when folded, and never changes launch scope. New accepted rows require planned_display_name plus planned_display_name_source=plex_destination_plan.v1; both the Queue-plan fingerprint and a recomputed accepted-membership digest bind this evidence. Raw, missing, blank, unversioned, contradictory, or tampered launch naming evidence blocks launch instead of becoming a verified label. For an older completed or parked run whose immutable accepted label predates that contract, the backend read projection may expose a different effective display_name only from exact same-item terminal output plus Completed/Pending evidence; accepted_display_name preserves the stored value and display_name_basis identifies the authority. Mismatched, partial, stale, future-dated, or nonterminal evidence remains legacy/unknown. No saved Run Monitor artifact is rewritten, and the WebView never cleans or infers a filename.
tests_added: Accepted Queue snapshots use New-PlexDestinationPlan filenames while raw source_path remains unchanged; force-rename changes both Queue-plan and accepted-membership fingerprints.

Browser monitor renders exactly 20 verified clean names, expands all 25 exact rows, supports End-key selection, leads accessible names and semantic announcements with the planned filename, retains fold/selection state on same-run refresh, preserves the exact focused row DOM node without a new focus event on unchanged refresh, retains active-worker focus in folded and expanded modes, re-announces a genuine active-to-quiet-to-same-active transition, and safely resets focus on run replacement.
Legacy or contradictory display-name evidence is labeled unknown/read-only and never presented as a verified naming plan.
Naming corpus covers screenshot-style YIFY, YTS, BONE, GalaxyRG265, Judas, SubsPlease, and ToonsHub release names.
Planner/pre-planner naming failures and raw, blank, unversioned, or contradictory naming evidence fail closed without source-leaf fallback.
Python and PowerShell recompute one canonical accepted-membership digest and reject changed planned-name evidence; a cross-runtime test vector locks canonical parity.

The standard mode=once Backend Queue journey passes Queue loaded through accepted fingerprint/run identity, stages, two workers, clean-name terminal/review handoff, run completion, reload, and fresh idle with blank Single File and unchanged source hashes.
Touchpoint ledger and root browser census include the Home disclosure with zero unclassified controls.
